```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
PKNCA::PKNCA.options(progress = FALSE)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Srinivas_2019_efavirenz_human"))$reference`
* Human model: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Srinivas_2019_efavirenz_human"))$description`
* Macaque model: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Srinivas_2019_efavirenz_monkey"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1111/cts.12620> (open access, PMC6510381)

Srinivas et al. built one eight-compartment structure (Figure 1) for oral
efavirenz in plasma, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and brain tissue, fitted it
first to eight rhesus macaques with plasma, CSF and brain tissue
concentrations, and then re-estimated it on sparse paired plasma / CSF samples
from 24 adults living with HIV. Brain tissue cannot be sampled in living
humans, so the human brain parameters are predictions: their initial estimates
came from the macaque fit (Vbrain allometrically scaled) and the CSF data were
used to refine them. The two fits have different parameter values and
different structures (the macaque model has a step increase in clearance
after 24 h), so they are packaged as two models:

* `Srinivas_2019_efavirenz_human` -- adults with HIV, 600 mg once daily.
* `Srinivas_2019_efavirenz_monkey` -- rhesus macaques, 200 mg once daily.

No erratum or correction was found for this article (Europe PMC, checked
2026-11-25).

# Population

```{r population}
pop_h <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Srinivas_2019_efavirenz_human"))$population
pop_m <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Srinivas_2019_efavirenz_monkey"))$population
str(pop_h)
str(pop_m)
```

Humans (Table 2): 24 participants of the THINC cohort on efavirenz-based
therapy, 3 treatment-naive (cohort A, median age 32 years, 65.8 kg) and 21
treatment-experienced with suppressed viral load (cohort B, median age 54
years, 71.0 kg); 5 women; 13 White and 11 African American. 29 paired plasma
and CSF samples, taken without a preselected time after dose.

Macaques (Methods): 8 adult rhesus macaques (4 uninfected, 4 infected with
RT-SHIVmac239 -- infection status did not change concentrations) dosed 200 mg
efavirenz orally once daily for 10 days with tenofovir, emtricitabine and
raltegravir. Plasma was sampled at 0, 4, 10 and 24 h after the first dose and
24 h after dosing on days 4, 6, 9 and 10; CSF and brain tissue (median of four
regions) were taken at necropsy only, 79 concentrations in all.

# Model structure

Figure 1 numbers the compartments: 1 depot, 2-4 transit, 5 central (plasma),
6 peripheral, 7 CSF, 8 brain tissue. The dose moves depot -> transit1 ->
transit2 -> transit3 at one rate constant TAU and from transit3 to central at
Ka. Plasma disposition is two-compartment with intercompartmental clearance Q
and linear clearance CL. CSF and brain tissue exchange with plasma and with
each other through four pairs of first-order rate constants acting on the
amount in the donor compartment, so a transfer such as Kplasma-brain removes
`Kplasma-brain * A5` from central and adds it to the brain amount. That
reading is the one that reproduces the paper's reported exposure ratios: with
the human values the typical brain:plasma AUC ratio is
`(Kplasma-brain / Kbrain-plasma) * V5 / Vbrain` = 3.45, against the published
median 3.6 (range 3.2-3.8).

In the macaques, the trough concentrations of four animals from day 4 onward
were 4- to 40-fold below the first-dose trough, and the authors added a
multiplier M on clearance: `CL/F = CL/F * M` for time > 24 h after the first
dose. This is encoded with the library's piecewise-clearance names --
`ltclchange` fixed at 24 h and `lcl_late = log(CL * M)` -- with the late arm
carrying both random effects, which is the same distribution as
`CL * M` with independent CL and M variability. Time in the macaque model must
therefore be measured from the first dose. M is not part of the human model
(Table 1 footnote a).

# Source trace

All values are Table 1 geometric means of the individual estimates, used as
typical values, with Table 1 CV% converted to log-normal variances
`omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2)`.

| Quantity | Model name | Macaque | Human | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CL/F (L/h) | `lcl` | 8.70 (CV 89.8%) | 12.37 (CV 58.5%) | Table 1 |
| V5/F (L) | `lvc` | 6.45 (51.2%) | 155.34 (39.1%) | Table 1 |
| Ka (1/h), transit3 -> central | `lka` | 0.183 (36.4%) | 0.135 (94.6%) | Table 1; Figure 1 |
| V6/F (L) | `lvp` | 14.6 (155.0%) | 405.4 (35.8%) | Table 1 |
| Q/F (L/h) | `lq` | 4.66 (89.1%) | 6.31 (142.0%) | Table 1 |
| TAU (1/h), depot -> transit chain | `lktr` | 0.95 (48.5%) | 1.00 (27.8%) | Table 1; Figure 1 |
| M (clearance multiplier after 24 h) | `lcl_late` = log(CL x M), `ltclchange` = log(24) fixed | 2.63 (103.0%) | not in model | Table 1 and footnote a; Results; Figure 1 legend |
| Kplasma-CSF (1/h) | `lk_central_csf` | 1.71E-06 (59.5%) | 4.27E-06 (88.8%) | Table 1 |
| KCSF-plasma (1/h) | `lk_csf_central` | 0.18 (27.3%) | 0.244 (26.0%) | Table 1 |
| Kplasma-brain (1/h) | `lk_central_brain` | 2.42E-03 (31.1%) | 2.00E-03 (30.2%) | Table 1 |
| Kbrain-plasma (1/h) | `lk_brain_central` | 0.15 (26.8%) | 0.175 (31.2%) | Table 1 |
| KCSF-brain (1/h) | `lk_csf_brain` | 2.56E-03 (36.0%) | 3.00E-03 (40.2%) | Table 1 |
| Kbrain-CSF (1/h) | `lk_brain_csf` | 5.58E-06 (68.2%) | 2.41E-06 (70.5%) | Table 1 |
| Vbrain/F (L) | `lv_brain` | 0.037 (21.8%) | 0.514 (25.1%) | Table 1 |
| VCSF/F (L), fixed | `lvcsf` | 0.015 | 0.15 | Table 1; Methods |
| Residual error | `propSd`, `addSd` (+ `_Ccsf`, `_Cbrain`) | fixed 0 | fixed 0 | Methods (additive + proportional, values not reported) |
| ODEs | `d/dt(...)` | -- | -- | Figure 1 |
| Concentrations | `Cc = central / vc`, `Ccsf = csf / vcsf`, `Cbrain = brain / v_brain` | -- | -- | Figure 1; Table 1 volumes |

# Human: steady-state simulation

A cohort of 200 virtual adults received 600 mg once daily for 8 weeks; the
last dosing interval is observed. The model has no covariates, so the cohort
needs no demographic draws.

```{r sim-human}
mod_h <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Srinivas_2019_efavirenz_human"))

n_h <- 200
n_days <- 56
tau <- 24
t_ss <- tau * (n_days - 1)

dose_h <- data.frame(
  id = rep(seq_len(n_h), each = n_days),
  time = rep((seq_len(n_days) - 1) * tau, n_h),
  amt = 600, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot", dvid = NA_integer_
)
# Two declared endpoints (Cc, Ccsf): every observation row nominates one with
# dvid; each row still returns Cc, Ccsf and Cbrain as columns.
obs_h <- expand.grid(id = seq_len(n_h), time = t_ss + seq(0, tau, by = 0.5)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = NA_character_, dvid = 1L)
ev_h <- dplyr::bind_rows(dose_h, obs_h) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))

rxode2::rxSetSeed(20190125)
sim_h <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_h, ev_h, returnType = "data.frame")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(tad = time - t_ss)

stopifnot(
  all(c("Cc", "Ccsf", "Cbrain") %in% names(sim_h)),
  all(rxode2::rxState(mod_h) %in% names(sim_h)),
  nrow(sim_h) == nrow(obs_h)
)
```

Steady state is reached well inside 8 weeks for the typical participant:

```{r ss-check}
typ_h <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod_h)
ev_typ <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  dose_h |> dplyr::filter(id == 1),
  data.frame(id = 1, time = seq(0, tau * n_days, by = 0.5), amt = 0, evid = 0L, dvid = 1L)
) |>
  dplyr::arrange(time, dplyr::desc(evid))
s_typ <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(typ_h, ev_typ, returnType = "data.frame"))
auc_trap <- function(x, y) sum(diff(x) * (head(y, -1) + tail(y, -1)) / 2)
auc_day <- function(d, col) {
  w <- s_typ[s_typ$time >= tau * (d - 1) & s_typ$time <= tau * d, ]
  auc_trap(w$time, w[[col]])
}
ss_ratio <- c(
  plasma = auc_day(n_days, "Cc") / auc_day(n_days - 1, "Cc"),
  brain = auc_day(n_days, "Cbrain") / auc_day(n_days - 1, "Cbrain")
)
ss_ratio
# Deterministic solve against itself: day 56 and day 55 exposures agree.
stopifnot(all(abs(ss_ratio - 1) < 0.01))
```

## Figure 3 -- visual predictive check in plasma, CSF and brain tissue

The published figure overlays the observed plasma and CSF samples (not
reproduced here) and three post-mortem brain tissue concentrations from the
National NeuroAIDS Tissue Consortium, printed in Table S2.

```{r figure-3, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 3.5}
nntc <- data.frame(
  matrix = "Brain tissue",
  tad = c(24, 21, 21),
  conc = c(1800, 8000, 3600)
)
vpc_h <- sim_h |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    id, tad,
    Plasma = Cc * 1000, CSF = Ccsf * 1000, `Brain tissue` = Cbrain * 1000
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(Plasma, CSF, `Brain tissue`), names_to = "matrix", values_to = "conc") |>
  dplyr::group_by(matrix, tad) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    p05 = quantile(conc, 0.05), p25 = quantile(conc, 0.25),
    p50 = median(conc), p75 = quantile(conc, 0.75), p95 = quantile(conc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(matrix = factor(matrix, levels = c("Plasma", "CSF", "Brain tissue")))

ggplot(vpc_h, aes(tad)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p50), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p25), linetype = "dashed", colour = "darkgreen") +
  geom_line(aes(y = p75), linetype = "dashed", colour = "darkgreen") +
  geom_line(aes(y = p05), linetype = "dashed", colour = "red") +
  geom_line(aes(y = p95), linetype = "dashed", colour = "red") +
  geom_point(
    data = dplyr::mutate(nntc, matrix = factor(matrix, levels = levels(vpc_h$matrix))),
    aes(y = conc), shape = 2, size = 2.5
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~matrix, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time after last dose (h)", y = "Efavirenz (ng/mL)",
    caption = paste(
      "Replicates Figure 3 of Srinivas 2019: median (solid), 25th/75th (green)",
      "and 5th/95th (red) percentiles at steady state; triangles are the",
      "Table S2 NNTC brain tissue concentrations."
    )
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

## PKNCA: steady-state exposure in each matrix

The final dosing interval is re-based to time 0 and analysed per matrix.

```{r pknca-human}
conc_h <- sim_h |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    id, time = tad, treatment = "EFV 600 mg QD",
    Plasma = Cc * 1000, CSF = Ccsf * 1000, Brain = Cbrain * 1000
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(Plasma, CSF, Brain), names_to = "matrix", values_to = "conc") |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(conc))
dose_nca_h <- conc_h |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, treatment, matrix) |>
  dplyr::mutate(time = 0, amt = 600)

o_conc_h <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_h, conc ~ time | treatment + matrix + id)
o_dose_h <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_nca_h, amt ~ time | treatment + matrix + id)
o_data_h <- PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  o_conc_h, o_dose_h,
  intervals = data.frame(
    start = 0, end = tau, auclast = TRUE, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE,
    cmin = TRUE, ctrough = TRUE, cav = TRUE
  )
)
nca_h <- as.data.frame(PKNCA::pk.nca(o_data_h))

nca_h_wide <- nca_h |>
  dplyr::select(id, treatment, matrix, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)

nca_h_wide |>
  dplyr::group_by(matrix) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    `AUC0-24 median (ng*h/mL)` = signif(median(auclast), 3),
    `AUC0-24 5th-95th` = paste(signif(quantile(auclast, c(0.05, 0.95)), 3), collapse = " - "),
    `C24 median (ng/mL)` = signif(median(ctrough), 3),
    `Cmax median (ng/mL)` = signif(median(cmax), 3),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Simulated steady-state exposure, 200 virtual adults, 600 mg once daily.")
```

## Comparison with the published predictions

The paper reports the model-predicted CSF and brain tissue concentrations
("flat", Results) and the brain:plasma and brain:CSF AUC0-24 ratios as
medians over the 24 participants' individual (posterior) predictions. The
simulated values below are medians over a population draw from the Table 1
geometric means and CVs, so close but not exact agreement is expected.

```{r nca-compare-human}
ratios_h <- nca_h_wide |>
  dplyr::select(id, matrix, auclast) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = matrix, values_from = auclast) |>
  dplyr::mutate(brain_plasma = Brain / Plasma, brain_csf = Brain / CSF)

sim_cmp_h <- nca_h_wide |>
  dplyr::filter(matrix %in% c("Brain", "CSF")) |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment, matrix) |>
  dplyr::summarise(ctrough = median(ctrough), auclast = median(auclast), .groups = "drop")
ref_cmp_h <- data.frame(
  treatment = "EFV 600 mg QD",
  matrix = c("Brain", "CSF"),
  # Results: brain tissue 8,000 ng/mL (2,300-29,000) and CSF 30 ng/mL (6-170).
  ctrough = c(8000, 30),
  # Conclusions: brain tissue AUC0-24 150,000 ng*h/mL; no CSF median printed.
  auclast = c(150000, NA)
)
cmp_h <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = sim_cmp_h,
  reference = ref_cmp_h,
  by = c("treatment", "matrix"),
  units = c(ctrough = "ng/mL", auclast = "ng*h/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(
  cmp_h,
  caption = paste(
    "Median simulated steady-state brain and CSF exposure against the values",
    "reported by Srinivas 2019. * marks a difference above 20%."
  )
)
```

The exposure ratios are not NCA parameters, so they are compared separately:

```{r ratio-compare-human}
ratio_tbl <- data.frame(
  ratio = c("Brain:plasma AUC0-24", "Brain:CSF AUC0-24"),
  published = c("3.6 (3.2-3.8)", "213 (23-834)"),
  sim_median = c(median(ratios_h$brain_plasma), median(ratios_h$brain_csf)),
  ref_median = c(3.6, 213)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = round(100 * (sim_median - ref_median) / ref_median, 1))
ratio_tbl |>
  dplyr::mutate(sim_median = as.character(signif(sim_median, 3))) |>
  dplyr::select(-ref_median) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Ratio" = ratio,
    "Published median (range)" = published,
    "Simulated median" = sim_median,
    "% diff" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Brain tissue exposure ratios (Srinivas 2019 Results).")
```

The two brain values sit within about 20% of the published figures, and the
CSF trough and both ratios within 10%. The 150,000 ng h/mL brain AUC is a
rounded figure from the Conclusions; the simulated median trough is below the
quoted 8,000 ng/mL because the published value is a median over 24
individual posterior predictions rather than a population draw. The simulated
5th-95th percentile ranges of AUC0-24 (table above) also overlap the
published ranges over the 24 participants: plasma 19,223-165,487, brain
61,908-576,048 and CSF 200-9,940 ng h/mL (Discussion).

```{r nca-gate-human}
# Structural gate on the centre of the distribution. The brain:plasma ratio
# depends only on Kplasma-brain, Kbrain-plasma, V5 and Vbrain, so a wrong rate
# constant, volume or flow direction moves it by far more than 15%.
pct <- function(sim, ref) 100 * (sim - ref) / ref
brain_sim <- sim_cmp_h[sim_cmp_h$matrix == "Brain", ]
csf_sim <- sim_cmp_h[sim_cmp_h$matrix == "CSF", ]
gate_h <- c(
  ratio_brain_plasma = ratio_tbl$pct_diff[1],
  ratio_brain_csf = ratio_tbl$pct_diff[2],
  auclast_brain = pct(brain_sim$auclast, 150000),
  ctrough_brain = pct(brain_sim$ctrough, 8000),
  ctrough_csf = pct(csf_sim$ctrough, 30)
)
round(gate_h, 1)
stopifnot(
  abs(gate_h[["ratio_brain_plasma"]]) < 15,
  abs(gate_h[["ratio_brain_csf"]]) < 30,
  abs(gate_h[["auclast_brain"]]) < 35,
  abs(gate_h[["ctrough_brain"]]) < 35,
  abs(gate_h[["ctrough_csf"]]) < 40
)
```

# Macaque: 10-day course

A cohort of 200 virtual macaques received 200 mg once daily for 10 days,
observed from the first dose to necropsy 24 h after the tenth dose (240 h).

```{r sim-monkey}
mod_m <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Srinivas_2019_efavirenz_monkey"))

n_m <- 200
dose_m <- data.frame(
  id = rep(seq_len(n_m), each = 10),
  time = rep((0:9) * tau, n_m),
  amt = 200, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot"
)
# Three declared endpoints (Cc, Ccsf, Cbrain): rxode2 already owns a modelled
# slot for each, so observation rows name one endpoint (cmt = "Cc"); every row
# still returns all three concentrations and every ODE state.
obs_m <- expand.grid(id = seq_len(n_m), time = seq(0, 240, by = 0.5)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "Cc")
ev_m <- dplyr::bind_rows(dose_m, obs_m) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))

rxode2::rxSetSeed(20190126)
sim_m <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_m, ev_m, returnType = "data.frame"))

# Guard: the dose still lands in depot (state 1) and the endpoint rows did not
# renumber the ODE states.
stopifnot(
  identical(rxode2::rxState(mod_m)[1:5], c("depot", "transit1", "transit2", "transit3", "central")),
  all(rxode2::rxState(mod_m) %in% names(sim_m)),
  all(c("Cc", "Ccsf", "Cbrain") %in% names(sim_m)),
  isTRUE(all.equal(sim_m$depot[sim_m$id == 1 & sim_m$time == 0], 200))
)
```

## Figure 2 -- plasma after the first dose and CSF / brain at steady state

```{r figure-2, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 3.5}
pi_m <- function(d, col, label) {
  d |>
    dplyr::group_by(t_plot) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      p05 = quantile(.data[[col]] * 1000, 0.05),
      p50 = median(.data[[col]] * 1000),
      p95 = quantile(.data[[col]] * 1000, 0.95),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    dplyr::mutate(panel = label)
}
fig2 <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  pi_m(dplyr::filter(sim_m, time > 0, time <= 24) |> dplyr::mutate(t_plot = time), "Cc",
       "(a) Plasma, first dose"),
  pi_m(dplyr::filter(sim_m, time >= 216) |> dplyr::mutate(t_plot = time - 216), "Ccsf",
       "(b) CSF, day 10"),
  pi_m(dplyr::filter(sim_m, time >= 216) |> dplyr::mutate(t_plot = time - 216), "Cbrain",
       "(c) Brain tissue, day 10")
)
ggplot(fig2, aes(t_plot)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p50)) +
  facet_wrap(~panel, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Efavirenz (ng/mL)",
    caption = paste(
      "Replicates Figure 2 of Srinivas 2019 as a population band (median and",
      "5th-95th percentiles) rather than the eight individual fits."
    )
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

## PKNCA: first dose and day 10

```{r pknca-monkey}
conc_m <- sim_m |>
  dplyr::filter(time <= 24 | time >= 216) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    treatment = ifelse(time <= 24, "Day 1", "Day 10"),
    time = ifelse(time <= 24, time, time - 216)
  ) |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    id, time, treatment,
    Plasma = Cc * 1000, CSF = Ccsf * 1000, Brain = Cbrain * 1000
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(Plasma, CSF, Brain), names_to = "matrix", values_to = "conc") |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(conc))
dose_nca_m <- conc_m |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, treatment, matrix) |>
  dplyr::mutate(time = 0, amt = 200)

o_data_m <- PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_m, conc ~ time | treatment + matrix + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_nca_m, amt ~ time | treatment + matrix + id),
  intervals = data.frame(
    start = 0, end = tau, auclast = TRUE, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, ctrough = TRUE
  )
)
nca_m_wide <- as.data.frame(PKNCA::pk.nca(o_data_m)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, treatment, matrix, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)

nca_m_wide |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment, matrix) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    `AUC0-24 median (ng*h/mL)` = signif(median(auclast), 3),
    `Cmax median (ng/mL)` = signif(median(cmax), 3),
    `Tmax median (h)` = median(tmax),
    `C24 median (ng/mL)` = signif(median(ctrough), 3),
    `C24 5th-95th` = paste(signif(quantile(ctrough, c(0.05, 0.95)), 3), collapse = " - "),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Simulated macaque exposure, 200 virtual animals, 200 mg once daily.")
```

## Comparison with the observed necropsy concentrations

The paper quotes observed (not model-predicted) necropsy concentrations: brain
tissue medians of 687-834 ng/g across the four regions (Results), about
775 ng/mL overall, CSF about 2 ng/mL and plasma about 200 ng/mL (Discussion);
Figure 4 plots the eight animals' observed troughs (plasma about
55-1,500 ng/mL, brain tissue about 4-fold higher).

```{r compare-monkey}
nec_sim <- nca_m_wide |>
  dplyr::filter(treatment == "Day 10") |>
  dplyr::group_by(matrix) |>
  dplyr::summarise(ctrough = median(ctrough), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::mutate(treatment = "Necropsy (240 h)")
nec_ref <- data.frame(
  treatment = "Necropsy (240 h)",
  matrix = c("Brain", "CSF", "Plasma"),
  # Discussion: brain tissue 775, CSF ~2 and plasma ~200 ng/mL in macaques.
  ctrough = c(775, 2, 200)
)
cmp_m <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nec_sim,
  reference = nec_ref,
  by = c("treatment", "matrix"),
  units = c(ctrough = "ng/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(
  cmp_m,
  caption = paste(
    "Median simulated necropsy concentrations against the observed values",
    "quoted by Srinivas 2019. * marks a difference above 20%."
  )
)
```

All three simulated medians are below the observed values, by about 30% in
brain tissue and by more in plasma and CSF. This follows from the published
parameterisation rather than from the encoding. The clearance step was seen
in only four of the eight animals (4- to 40-fold lower troughs from day 4),
and the other four had none. Table 1 summarises M over all eight animals as a
geometric mean of 2.63 (median 2.07, CV 103%). A log-normal M centred there
gives the median virtual animal most of the clearance increase. The simulated
day-1 plasma trough, which comes before the step, has a median of
`r signif(median(dplyr::filter(nca_m_wide, treatment == "Day 1", matrix == "Plasma")$ctrough), 3)`
ng/mL, in line with the about 200 ng/mL the paper quotes. At steady state,
the shapes of the simulated CSF and brain tissue profiles (a rise to a peak
near 10 h and a fall back by 24 h) match the individual fits in Figure 2b-c.

```{r gate-monkey}
# Order-of-magnitude gate on the observed brain tissue concentration: the
# median simulated necropsy value lies within a factor of 2 of the observed
# ~775 ng/mL and inside the observed regional range (190-2,440 ng/g).
brain_nec <- nec_sim$ctrough[nec_sim$matrix == "Brain"]
day1_plasma <- median(dplyr::filter(nca_m_wide, treatment == "Day 1", matrix == "Plasma")$ctrough)
stopifnot(
  brain_nec > 775 / 2, brain_nec < 775 * 2,
  brain_nec > 190, brain_nec < 2440,
  # Pre-step plasma trough: within a factor of 2 of the quoted ~200 ng/mL.
  day1_plasma > 100, day1_plasma < 400
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Typical values are geometric means of individual estimates.** The paper
  fits each species by iterative two-stage (IT2S) Bayesian estimation in
  ADAPT 5 and reports, per parameter, the geometric mean, median and CV% of
  the individual estimates (Table 1; Statistical analysis: "PK estimates are
  presented as geometric means"). The geometric means are used as typical
  values, and the CV% as between-subject variability through
  `omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2)`. For a few human parameters the median differs
  markedly from the geometric mean (Ka 0.025 vs 0.135 1/h, Q/F 28.33 vs
  6.31 L/h, V6/F 200 vs 405 L), which indicates a skewed distribution over 24
  sparsely sampled participants; the log-normal summary does not capture that
  skew.
* **No covariances.** None are reported, so all random effects are
  independent.
* **Residual error is unreported.** Methods describe a variance model with
  additive and proportional components, while Results describe the error
  model as log-normal; no magnitudes are given. Both additive and
  proportional components are encoded for each observed matrix and fixed at
  zero, so simulations carry between-subject variability only. Brain tissue
  was not measured in humans, so the human model declares no brain residual
  error and `Cbrain` is a derived output.
* **Rate constants act on amounts.** The paper names the CNS transfers as
  rate constants (1/h) without writing the equations. First-order transfer of
  the donor-compartment amount is the reading under which the human typical
  brain:plasma AUC ratio (3.45) matches the published 3.6 and the CSF:plasma
  ratio (about 0.018) matches the reported CSF (30 ng/mL) and plasma
  (2,100 ng/mL) levels.
* **Absorption chain.** Following Figure 1, TAU governs depot -> transit1,
  transit1 -> transit2 and transit2 -> transit3, and Ka governs
  transit3 -> central.
* **Macaque clearance step.** "If time > 24 hours, then CL/F = CL/F x M" is
  encoded as a step at 24 h after the first dose with the Table 1 geometric
  mean M = 2.63 applied to every animal. In the study only four of the eight
  animals showed the lowered troughs; the M variability (CV 103%) is how the
  model spreads the effect across animals, so individual virtual macaques
  range from little change to a large increase. Because the observed effect
  was bimodal (present or absent), the median virtual animal at necropsy has
  lower plasma, CSF and brain concentrations than the median observed animal
  (see the macaque comparison above).
* **Apparent volumes and rate constants.** All volumes are apparent (/F)
  because bioavailability was not estimated; VCSF is fixed at 0.015 L
  (macaque, from the literature) and 0.15 L (human, allometrically scaled),
  and Vbrain is conditioned on it.
* **Figure comparisons are population bands.** The paper's Figure 2 shows the
  eight individual macaque fits and Figure 3 a 1,000-replicate VPC with
  observed data overlaid; neither the individual parameters nor the observed
  data are published, so the vignette shows population bands from the Table 1
  distribution.
